citations.quote:
Fix real parameters $m>0$ and $q_e,q_m$ with $q_e^2+q_m^2=m^2$, and use the selected ingoing dyonic Reissner–Nordström metric on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{in}}=\mathbb R_v\times(0,\infty)_r\times S^2$ with signature $(-,+,+,+)$:

$$g=-D(r)\,dv^2+2\,dv\,dr+r^2\gamma_{S^2},\qquad D(r)=\left(1-\frac mr\right)^2.$$

Here $\gamma_{S^2}$ is the metric induced on the unit sphere $S^2\subset\mathbb R^3$ by the Euclidean metric, and $\omega_{S^2}$ is its outward area form. The coordinates $v,r$ and parameters $m,q_e,q_m$ have units of metres; angular coordinates are dimensionless. The displayed Maxwell two-form uses the supplied geometric normalization, with no additional SI normalization: its $vr$ coordinate component has units $\mathrm m^{-1}$ and its angular components have units $\mathrm m$. In the supplied ingoing RN background with mass parameter $M=m$, the fixed Maxwell two-form is

$$\mathcal F_{\mathrm{in}}=-q_e r^{-2}\,dv\wedge dr+q_m\omega_{S^2}.$$

Use the unique torsion-free, $g$-compatible connection; in every smooth chart its coefficients are $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12g^{ad}(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc})$ and are smooth. For the horizon-data result, set $M=m$, $Q^2=q_e^2+q_m^2=M^2$ and $f(r):=1-2M/r+Q^2/r^2=D(r)$. It states that $\xi=\partial_v$ obeys $\mathcal L_\xi g=0$ and is normalized by $g(\xi,\xi)\to-1$ as $r\to\infty$; at $r=M$, $g^{-1}(dr,dr)=f(M)=0$, $\xi^\flat=dr$, and $\xi$ is tangent to the level. Thus $r=m$ is the local Killing horizon generated by $\xi$, with signed surface gravity fixed by $d(g(\xi,\xi))=-2\kappa_H\xi^\flat$ and equal to $\kappa_H=f'(M)/2=0$ (units $\mathrm m^{-1}$). No maximal-extension or global event-horizon assertion is included. The metric and displayed Maxwell field are fixed. A neutral test scalar has no electromagnetic gauge coupling or scalar coupling to that field, and does not source either background.

A reduced spherical scalar profile is a real function $\psi:\mathbb R_v\times(0,\infty)_r\to\mathbb R$ whose coordinate partial derivatives through total order three are continuous. Its full scalar on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{in}}$ is the spherical lift $\widetilde\psi(v,r,\omega):=\psi(v,r)$; in radial formulas we use $\psi(v,r)$ for the reduced profile, and the notation $\Box_g\psi=0$ means $\Box_g\widetilde\psi=0$. For a $C^3$ scalar lift, define the extension of the smooth-scalar wave operator by the trace of its $C^1$ scalar Hessian,

$$\Box_g\widetilde\psi:=g^{ab}\bigl(\partial_a\partial_b\widetilde\psi-\Gamma^c{}_{ab}\partial_c\widetilde\psi\bigr).$$

The second-order chain rule and the connection-coefficient transformation law make these components a covariant $2$-tensor, so the trace is chart independent and $C^1$. This agrees with the supplied smooth-scalar definition when the lift is smooth. In every smooth chart, with $w=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$, metric compatibility and the density formula give

$$\Box_g\widetilde\psi=\frac1w\partial_a\bigl(wg^{ab}\partial_b\widetilde\psi\bigr).$$

For the spherical lift in an angular chart, $w=r^2\sqrt{\det(\gamma_{AB})}$ and this becomes

$$\Box_g\widetilde\psi=\frac1{r^2}\left[\partial_v(r^2\partial_r\psi)+\partial_r\!\left(r^2(\partial_v\psi+D\partial_r\psi)\right)\right].$$

The density identity used here is stated for smooth vector fields, but its coordinate proof uses only first derivatives of their components and the product rule; it therefore holds for $C^1$ vector fields as well. Here $g^{ab}\partial_b\widetilde\psi$ is $C^2$, so the formula is defined and $\Box_g\widetilde\psi$ is $C^1$. In particular the wave equation can be differentiated once in $r$ for a $C^3$ profile. Set $\phi(v,r)=r\psi(v,r)$ and take every $\partial_r$ derivative in this regular ingoing chart. If $[\psi]$ denotes the arbitrary scalar-field unit, then $[\phi]=[\psi]\,\mathrm m$.

Fix $m>0$ and real $q_e,q_m$ with $q_e^2+q_m^2=m^2$, and take the ingoing extremal RN metric and coordinates specified by the spherical test-scalar definition. Let $\psi$ be any admissible neutral spherical $C^3$ solution of $\Box_g\psi=0$, set $\phi=r\psi$, and define its spherical horizon charge by

$$H_\psi(v):=\partial_r\phi(v,m).$$

Then $H_\psi$ is constant for all $v\in\mathbb R$. If this constant is nonzero, the regular ingoing-chart transverse derivative $\partial_r\phi(v,m)$ is nonzero and does not tend to zero along the horizon. If $[\psi]$ is the scalar-field unit, then $[H_\psi]=[\psi]$. This is a local fixed-background statement and asserts no global decay or nonlinear instability.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $(U,x)$ be a
smooth chart, and define the local **metric density** by
$w:=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$ on $U$, using the matrix of metric components
in this chart. This definition requires no orientation or volume form. Write
$g^{ab}$ for the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) and
$\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}$ for the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in the chart.

**(a) Derivative of the density.** At every point of $U$,

$$\partial_a w=\tfrac12\,w\,g^{bc}\,\partial_a g_{bc}.$$

**(b) Trace of the Christoffel symbols.** At every point of $U$,

$$\Gamma^{b}{}_{ba}=w^{-1}\partial_a w .$$

**(c) Divergence formula.** For every smooth vector field $J$ on $M$, at every
point of $U$,

$$\nabla_aJ^a=\partial_aJ^a+\Gamma^{a}{}_{ab}J^b=w^{-1}\partial_a\bigl(w\,J^a\bigr),$$

where $\nabla_aJ^a=g^{ab}\nabla_bJ_a$ is the divergence of $J$ contracted with
the metric and $J^a$ are the components of $J$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).

The identity of (c) is a chart formula for a chart-independent scalar: the
right-hand side is independent of the chart, as the left-hand side is.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be order-convex with at least two elements
([[def-interval]]) and let $f : I \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $I$
([[def-continuity-real]]). Call $G : I \to \mathbb{R}$ a **primitive of $f$ on
$I$** when $G$ is differentiable at every point of $I$ as a function on $I$ with
$G' = f$ there ([[def-derivative]]). Then:

1. **Existence.** Fix $c_0 \in I$. The function
   $$F : I \to \mathbb{R}, \qquad F(x) \;:=\; \int_{c_0}^x f$$
   is defined at every $x \in I$ ([[def-oriented-integral]],
   [[def-the-integral-function]]) and is a primitive of $f$ on $I$.
2. **Uniqueness up to a constant.** If $G_1$ and $G_2$ are primitives of $f$ on
   $I$ then there is a real $k$ with $G_1(x) = G_2(x) + k$ for every $x \in I$.
3. **Evaluation.** If $a, b \in I$ with $a < b$ and $G$ is any primitive of $f$
   on $I$, then
   $$\int_a^b f \;=\; G(b) - G(a) .$$

proof.** An integrable function need not have a primitive, and a function with a
primitive need not be integrable; this corollary is precisely the intersection
where both fundamental theorems apply, and both witnesses are on the companion
page.

Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$ and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be
continuous on $[a,b]$ (Continuity of $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ at a point of $A$ and on $A$: the $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ condition, its agreement with $\lim_{x \to c} f(x) = f(c)$ at a limit point, and continuity at an isolated point, Intervals of $\mathbb{R}$: the nine order-convex forms, nondegeneracy, and length) and
differentiable at every point of $(a,b)$ as a function on $[a,b]$
(The derivative $f'(c) = \lim_{x \to c} \frac{f(x) - f(c)}{x - c}$ of $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ at a point $c \in A$ that is a limit point of $A$, and differentiability on a set). Then there is $c \in (a,b)$ with

$$f(b) - f(a) \;=\; f'(c)\,(b - a) .$$

Equivalently, since $b - a \ne 0$, there is $c \in (a,b)$ at which
$f'(c) = \bigl(f(b)-f(a)\bigr)/(b-a)$: the derivative somewhere inside equals
the average rate of change across the whole interval.

every point of $(a,b)$ alone does not suffice: a function on $[0,1]$,
differentiable at every point of $(0,1)$ with derivative constantly $1$, for
which no $c$ works, is exhibited later on this page as a false statement, and
the companion page works the same witness out in full.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim:
In a local sphere chart with angular metric components $\gamma_{AB}$, the inverse of the ingoing $(v,r)$ metric block is $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&D\end{pmatrix}$ and the full density is $w=r^2\sqrt{\det(\gamma_{AB})}$. For $J^a=g^{ab}\partial_b\widetilde\psi$, spherical symmetry gives $J^v=\psi_r$, $J^r=\psi_v+D\psi_r$, and $J^A=0$. This vector field is $C^2$, so [F3] applies. By [F1], [F4] and metric compatibility, $\Box_g\widetilde\psi=\nabla_aJ^a$. Applying the density formula and cancelling the angular density, which is independent of $v,r$, yields
$$0=\Box_g\widetilde\psi=\frac1{r^2}\left[\partial_v(r^2\psi_r)+\partial_r\!\left(r^2(\psi_v+D\psi_r)\right)\right].$$
Expanding and using equality of the continuous mixed partials gives $2r^2\psi_{vr}+2r\psi_v+\partial_r(r^2D\psi_r)=0$. With $\phi=r\psi$, the identities $2r^2\psi_{vr}+2r\psi_v=2r\phi_{vr}$ and $r^2D\psi_r=D(r\phi_r-\phi)$ reduce this to
$$2\phi_{vr}+D\phi_{rr}+D'\phi_r-\frac{D'}r\phi=0.$$

Let $f(v):=\phi(v,m)$, which is continuous and tends to zero by [A2], and define $F(v):=\int_{v_0}^v f(s)\,ds$ for any fixed $v_0\in\mathbb R$. By [F5], $F$ exists and $F'=f$. Given $\varepsilon>0$, choose $S\ge v_0$ so that $|f(s)|<\varepsilon$ for every $s\ge S$. For each $v>S$, the mean value theorem [F6] on $[S,v]$ gives a $c\in(S,v)$ with $F(v)-F(S)=f(c)(v-S)$; hence
$$\left|\frac{F(v)}v\right|\le\frac{|F(S)|}{v}+\varepsilon\frac{v-S}{v}.$$
Taking $v\to+\infty$ gives $\limsup |F(v)/v|\le\varepsilon$. Since $\varepsilon$ was arbitrary, $F(v)/v\to0$.

Differentiate the equation in step 1.1 once in $r$, which is permitted because $\phi$ is $C^3$. The result is
$$2\phi_{vrr}+D\phi_{rrr}+2D'\phi_{rr}+\left(D''-\frac{D'}r\right)\phi_r-\left(\frac{D''}r-\frac{D'}{r^2}\right)\phi=0.$$
Direct differentiation gives $D(m)=D'(m)=0$ and $D''(m)=2/m^2$. Evaluating at $r=m$ and using [F2] therefore yields the exact horizon transport identity
$$\partial_v\phi_{rr}(v,m)=-\frac{H}{m^2}+\frac{\phi(v,m)}{m^3}.$$

Define $P(v):=-H(v-v_0)/m^2+F(v)/m^3$ and $G(v):=\phi_{rr}(v,m)$. By [F5], $F'(v)=\phi(v,m)$, so $P'(v)=-H/m^2+\phi(v,m)/m^3=G'(v)$ by step 2.1. Both $P$ and $G$ are continuous on $[v_0,\infty)$ and differentiable on its interior; [F7] makes $G-P$ constant there. Since $P(v_0)=0$, this gives
$$\phi_{rr}(v,m)-\phi_{rr}(v_0,m)=-\frac{H}{m^2}(v-v_0)+\frac{F(v)}{m^3}.$$
Divide by $v$ and use step 1.2; the fixed terms $\phi_{rr}(v_0,m)/v$ and $Hv_0/(m^2v)$ tend to zero, while $F(v)/(m^3v)\to0$. Therefore $\phi_{rr}(v,m)/v\to-H/m^2$. Since $H\ne0$, the limit is nonzero and its absolute value is $|H|/m^2$, proving the stated linear growth.

Fix real parameters $m>0$ and $q_e,q_m$ with $q_e^2+q_m^2=m^2$, and use the selected ingoing dyonic Reissner–Nordström metric on $\mathbb R_v\times(0,\infty)_r\times S^2$ with signature $(-,+,+,+)$:

$$g=-D(r)\,dv^2+2\,dv\,dr+r^2\gamma_{S^2},\qquad D(r)=\left(1-\frac mr\right)^2.$$

Here $\gamma_{S^2}$ is the unit round metric, $v,r,m,q_e,q_m$ have units of metres, and angles are dimensionless. The surface $r=m$ is the selected local degenerate Killing horizon; no maximal extension or global event-horizon assertion is included. A neutral spherical test scalar is a real function $\psi:\mathbb R_v\times(0,\infty)_r\to\mathbb R$ independent of the sphere variable, whose coordinate partial derivatives through total order three are continuous, and which satisfies $\Box_g\psi=0$, where $\Box_g\psi=g^{ab}\nabla_a\nabla_b\psi$ is the metric trace of the scalar Hessian for the metric-selected connection. Neutral means no electromagnetic gauge coupling occurs in this equation; test means the metric and Maxwell field are fixed and are not sourced by $\psi$. Set $\phi(v,r)=r\psi(v,r)$ and take all $\partial_r$ derivatives in this regular ingoing chart. If $[\psi]$ denotes the arbitrary scalar-field unit, then $[\phi]=[\psi]\,\mathrm m$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $(U,x)$ be a
smooth chart, and define the local **metric density** by
$w:=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$ on $U$, using the matrix of metric components
in this chart. This definition requires no orientation or volume form. Write
$g^{ab}$ for the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) and
$\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}$ for the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in the chart.

**(a) Derivative of the density.** At every point of $U$,

$$\partial_a w=\tfrac12\,w\,g^{bc}\,\partial_a g_{bc}.$$

**(b) Trace of the Christoffel symbols.** At every point of $U$,

$$\Gamma^{b}{}_{ba}=w^{-1}\partial_a w .$$

**(c) Divergence formula.** For every smooth vector field $J$ on $M$, at every
point of $U$,

$$\nabla_aJ^a=\partial_aJ^a+\Gamma^{a}{}_{ab}J^b=w^{-1}\partial_a\bigl(w\,J^a\bigr),$$

where $\nabla_aJ^a=g^{ab}\nabla_bJ_a$ is the divergence of $J$ contracted with
the metric and $J^a$ are the components of $J$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).

The identity of (c) is a chart formula for a chart-independent scalar: the
right-hand side is independent of the chart, as the left-hand side is.

Let $\psi$ be any admissible neutral spherical $C^3$ solution of $\Box_g\psi=0$, set $\phi=r\psi$, and define its spherical horizon charge by

$$H_\psi(v):=\partial_r\phi(v,m).$$

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $M>0$ and $Q\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<|Q|<M$. Put
$$r_\pm:=M\pm\sqrt{M^2-Q^2},\qquad f(r):=1-\frac{2M}{r}+\frac{Q^2}{r^2},\qquad r>r_+.$$
Use the static exterior
$\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ext}}=\mathbb R_t\times(r_+,\infty)_r\times S^2$
with the electric specialization $q_e=Q$, $q_m=0$, and $t=x^0$ of the
Reissner--Nordström metric and potential fixed in the preceding definition.
Thus
$$g=-f\,dt^2+f^{-1}dr^2+r^2\gamma_{S^2},\qquad A=-\frac Qr\,dt,\qquad A_t\longrightarrow0\quad(r\longrightarrow\infty).$$
Here $r_+$ is the positive outer root in the selected local model, not a claim
about an event horizon in a maximal spacetime. Set
$\Phi_H:=Q/r_+=A_t(\infty)-A_t(r_+)$ for this gauge.

For a complex scalar function $\psi$ in this fixed trivialization and a real
coupling $e$, put $D_a\psi:=(\partial_a-ieA_a)\psi$. Define the massless
charged wave operator in the static chart by
$$\Box_{g,A}\psi:=-f^{-1}D_t^2\psi+\frac1{r^2}\partial_r\!\left(r^2f\,\partial_r\psi\right)+\frac1{r^2}\Delta_{\gamma_{S^2}}\psi,\qquad D_t=\partial_t+\frac{ieQ}{r}.$$
The equation used here is $\Box_{g,A}\psi=0$; it is a fixed-background,
minimally coupled test-field equation and does not evolve or source $g$ or $A$.

Let $e\in\mathbb R$, $\omega>0$, and $\ell\in\mathbb N_0$. Supply a smooth
real function $Y:S^2\to\mathbb R$ satisfying
$$\int_{S^2}Y^2\,d\omega_{S^2}=1,\qquad \Delta_{\gamma_{S^2}}Y=-\ell(\ell+1)Y.$$
No existence assertion about $Y$ is made. Use the tortoise coordinate
$$r_*(r):=\int_{2r_+}^{r}f(\rho)^{-1}\,d\rho,$$
which is strictly increasing because $f>0$ on the exterior. Under the
subextremal hypotheses the supplied RN scalar-coordinate result proves that
$r_*$ is a smooth coordinate from $(r_+,\infty)$ onto $\mathbb R$; hence
$r_*\to-\infty$ as $r\downarrow r_+$ and $r_*\to+\infty$ as $r\to\infty$.
A separated mode has the form
$$\psi(t,r,\Omega)=A_{\mathrm{in}}e^{-i\omega t}Y(\Omega)\frac{u(r_*)}{r},$$
where $A_{\mathrm{in}}\ne0$ is a fixed incident amplitude with units
$[\psi]\,\mathrm m$, and the normalized complex radial function $u$ and its
reflection and transmission coefficients are dimensionless.

Write $\omega_H:=\omega-e\Phi_H=\omega-eQ/r_+$ and, for any reference length
$L>0$, define the Coulomb phase
$$\Theta(r_*):=\omega r_*-eQ\log(r/L),\qquad \Theta'(r_*):=\omega-\frac{eQf(r)}r.$$
A normalized scattering solution is a smooth radial solution of
$\Box_{g,A}\psi=0$ for which, for some $R,T\in\mathbb C$,
$$u=e^{-i\Theta}+R e^{i\Theta}+o(1),\qquad \partial_{r_*}u=-i\Theta'e^{-i\Theta}+i\Theta'R e^{i\Theta}+o(1)\quad(r\longrightarrow\infty),$$
and
$$u=T e^{-i\omega_Hr_*}+o(1),\qquad \partial_{r_*}u=-i\omega_HTe^{-i\omega_Hr_*}+o(1)\quad(r\downarrow r_+).$$
The error terms tend to zero in the indicated limits. These boundary
conditions prescribe unit incoming amplitude at infinity and only the
ingoing branch at the future horizon. They define admissible scattering data;
they assert neither existence nor uniqueness of such a solution.

The logarithm in $\Theta$ is required by the long-range term
$-2\omega eQ/r$ in the asymptotic radial coefficient. Changing $L$ changes
constant phases, not flux magnitudes. A constant gauge shift changes the
frequency label, so the threshold uses the potential difference
$\Phi_H$, not an absolute value of $A_t$.

Use geometric units $G=c=1$ and length coordinates, with
$[t]=[r]=[r_*]=[M]=[Q]=[L]=\mathrm m$,
$[e]=[\omega]=\mathrm m^{-1}$, $f$ dimensionless, and $A_t$ dimensionless;
then $\Theta$ is dimensionless and each term in $\Box_{g,A}$ has units
$[\psi]\,\mathrm m^{-2}$. The coupling $e$ is the charge coupling in the
chosen field normalization; restoring SI units requires restoring the
corresponding field normalization and the charge-over-$\hbar$ coupling.
This definition excludes scalar mass, magnetic charge, mirrors, anti-de Sitter
boundaries, bound states, and complex-frequency quasinormal boundary conditions.
A scalar mass would change the propagating infinity wave number to
$\sqrt{\omega^2-\mu^2}$ and requires a different scattering normalization.
Complex-frequency quasinormal modes form a distinct non-self-adjoint spectral
problem and are not covered by the real-frequency Wronskian identity.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ have the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold structure, signature $(-,+,+,+)$, metric-selected connection $\nabla^g$, and length-coordinate convention of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Let $A\in\Omega^1(M)$ be a supplied smooth real one-form, let $e\in\mathbb R$ be a fixed real coupling, and let $\psi\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb C)$ be a smooth complex-valued function. In the length-coordinate convention, assign dimensionless components to $A_a$ and unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$ to $e$, so $eA_a$ has derivative unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$; assign $\psi$ an arbitrary fixed unit $[\psi]$. Define the complex covector

$$D_a\psi:=\nabla^g_a\psi-ieA_a\psi.$$

Since $\psi$ is a scalar, $\nabla^g_a\psi=\partial_a\psi$. Define the real symmetric covariant tensor

$$\mathsf T_{ab}[\psi;g,A,e]:=\overline{D_a\psi}\,D_b\psi+\overline{D_b\psi}\,D_a\psi-g_{ab}g^{cd}\overline{D_c\psi}\,D_d\psi,$$

with indices raised using $g^{-1}$. Its covariant components have unit $[\psi]^2\mathrm m^{-2}$. This is a mathematical tensor assignment. Its interpretation as a stress-energy tensor, and any field equation or conservation law, require a separate physical model.

derivations.claim:
Since $A_t=-Q/r$ and $\omega>0$, the time derivative satisfies $D_t\psi=-i\omega\psi+o(r^{-1})$. Using $D^r=f\partial_r=\partial_{r_*}$ and $\partial_{r_*}(u/r)=u'/r-fu/r^2$, the differentiated asymptotics and $\Theta'\to\omega$ give
$$\psi=\frac{A_{\mathrm{in}}e^{-i\omega t}Y}{r}\left(e^{-i\Theta}+Re^{i\Theta}\right)+o(r^{-1}),\qquad D^r\psi=\frac{A_{\mathrm{in}}e^{-i\omega t}Y}{r}\left(-i\omega e^{-i\Theta}+i\omega Re^{i\Theta}\right)+o(r^{-1}).$$

Since $g^r{}_t=0$, [F2] gives $\mathsf T^r{}_t=2\operatorname{Re}(\overline{D^r\psi}D_t\psi)$. Substitution of step 1.1 gives the diagonal terms $\omega^2(1-|R|^2)$; the cross terms are $z-\overline z$ for $z=\omega^2R e^{2i\Theta}$ and have zero real part. Integrating $Y^2$ over the sphere and taking $r\to\infty$ therefore gives the net outward flux $\mathcal P(r)\to2\omega^2|A_{\mathrm{in}}|^2(|R|^2-1)$.

For the incoming component, $D^r\psi_{\mathrm{in}}=-i\omega\psi_{\mathrm{in}}+o(r^{-1})$ and $D_t\psi_{\mathrm{in}}=-i\omega\psi_{\mathrm{in}}+o(r^{-1})$, so $\mathsf T^r{}_t[\psi_{\mathrm{in}}]=2\omega^2|\psi_{\mathrm{in}}|^2+o(r^{-2})$; its positive inward magnitude is $2\omega^2|A_{\mathrm{in}}|^2$ after sphere integration. For the reflected component, $D^r\psi_{\mathrm{ref}}=i\omega\psi_{\mathrm{ref}}+o(r^{-1})$ while $D_t\psi_{\mathrm{ref}}=-i\omega\psi_{\mathrm{ref}}+o(r^{-1})$, so its nonnegative outward magnitude is $2\omega^2|A_{\mathrm{in}}|^2|R|^2$. Their ratio is $|R|^2$ because $\omega>0$ and $A_{\mathrm{in}}\ne0$.

boundaries.reason: The conditional statement assumes an admitted mode with nonzero incident amplitude.
The hypotheses require $omega>0$ and $A_{\mathrm{in}}\ne0$; zero incident frequency/amplitude is excluded.

boundaries.evidence: At the unit-reflection boundary $|R|=1$, step 3.1 gives equal positive incoming and reflected magnitudes, hence ratio one.

boundaries.reason: The fixed subextremal exterior is nondegenerate in the stated open region and $omega>0$ keeps the incident flux positive.
The statement assumes $omega>0$ and makes no zero-frequency limit claim.

boundaries.evidence: The mode and harmonic are supplied; steps 1.1–3.1 make no selection from a family.

boundaries.reason: The item proves a flux formula, not a biconditional.
The item proves a flux formula, not a converse.

citations.quote:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the tangent-bundle smooth structure of the
Lorentzian conventions.

Let $M>0$ and $a\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $|a|<M$, and put
$r_\pm:=M\pm\sqrt{M^2-a^2}$.

Let $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}:=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$ carry the
product smooth structure, where $S^2=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:x^2+y^2+z^2=1\}$
has its usual smooth structure and round metric $\gamma_{S^2}$. Let
$\pi:\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}\to S^2$ be the third projection, let $\xi$ be the
smooth rotation field on $S^2$ generated by $(x,y,z)\mapsto(-y,x,0)$, and put
$\gamma:=\pi^*\gamma_{S^2}$ and
$\xi^\flat:=\pi^*(\gamma_{S^2}(\xi,\cdot))$. Let $t,r$ be the first and
second coordinate functions on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$, and let
$\zeta:=z\circ\pi$ be the third Euclidean coordinate on the sphere factor.
Define the global smooth functions

$$\Sigma:=r^2+a^2\zeta^2,\qquad \Delta:=r^2-2Mr+a^2.$$

On a polar chart $0<\theta<\pi$, $\phi\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, one has
$\zeta=\cos\theta$, $\Sigma=r^2+a^2\cos^2\theta$,
$\gamma=d\theta^2+\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2$, and
$\xi^\flat=\sin^2\theta\,d\phi$.

Define the symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $g$ globally on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$
by

$$g=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt\otimes dt+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr\otimes dr+\Sigma\gamma+\frac{a^2(\Sigma+2Mr)}{\Sigma}\,\xi^\flat\otimes\xi^\flat-\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma}\left(dt\otimes\xi^\flat+\xi^\flat\otimes dt\right).$$

Its Boyer-Lindquist line element on the polar chart is

$$ds^2=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt^2-\frac{4Mar\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\,dt\,d\phi+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr^2+\Sigma\,d\theta^2+\frac{(r^2+a^2)^2-a^2\Delta\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2.$$

The displayed cross term is $2g_{t\phi}\,dt\,d\phi$. This definition makes
no nondegeneracy or signature claim; Lorentzian signature and a time orientation
are established separately.

For $M>0$, $|a|<M$, and the Kerr exterior tensor datum, define
$T:=\partial_t$, $\Phi:=\xi$, $A:=r^2+a^2$, and $q:=\gamma(\xi,\xi)$.
The global vector field
$$N:=\frac{A^2-a^2\Delta q}{\Sigma\Delta}\,T+\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma\Delta}\,\Phi$$
is smooth; the tensor $g$ is smooth, symmetric, nondegenerate, and has
signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on all of
$\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$; and
$N=-\sharp_g(dt)$ is timelike. Thus $N$ defines a time orientation of this
Lorentzian four-manifold.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. Tensoriality of $R$ is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a).
Lowering its output slot with the smooth metric and contracting with the
smooth inverse metric are intrinsic tensor operations
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] clauses (b)-(c),
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]]). Thus these formulas give smooth
fields of types $(0,4)$, $(0,2)$, $(0,0)$ and $(0,2)$, respectively,
independent of the chart. Symmetry of $\operatorname{Ric}$ and $G$ is proved
separately in [[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clause (d).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let $R$ be
the curvature operator of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
with components $R^a{}_{bcd}$ in a chart.

**(a) Tensoriality.** For all smooth functions $f$ on $M$ and smooth vector
fields $X,Y,Z$ on a common domain, $R(X,Y)Z=-R(Y,X)Z$ and
$$R(fX,Y)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,fY)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,Y)(fZ)=fR(X,Y)Z .$$
Consequently, for every $p\in M$, the value $R(X,Y)Z|_p$ depends only on
$X_p,Y_p,Z_p$, and $R$ is a smooth tensor field of type $(1,3)$ on $M$ whose
components in every smooth chart are the functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ of
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]] clause (b).

**(b) Coordinate formula.** In every smooth chart $(U,x)$ with Christoffel
symbols $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ of $\nabla$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]),
$$R^a{}_{bcd}=\partial_c\Gamma^a{}_{db}-\partial_d\Gamma^a{}_{cb} +\sum_e\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{ce}\Gamma^e{}_{db}-\Gamma^a{}_{de}\Gamma^e{}_{cb}\bigr)$$
on $U$, for all $a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2,3\}$.

**(c) Point-normal formula.** If the chart is point-normal at $p$, that is
$g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}$, $\partial_ag_{bc}(p)=0$ and $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(p)=0$
([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]), then, writing
$g_{ad,bc}:=\partial_b\partial_cg_{ad}$,
$$R_{abcd}(p)=\tfrac12\bigl(g_{ad,bc}+g_{bc,ad}-g_{bd,ac}-g_{ac,bd}\bigr)(p) .$$
Equivalently, $R^a{}_{bcd}(p)=\tfrac12\,g^{ae}(p)\bigl(\partial_b\partial_cg_{ed}
+\partial_e\partial_dg_{bc}-\partial_e\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_b\partial_dg_{ec}\bigr)(p)$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Work first on a polar chart with $0<\theta<\pi$ and change angular coordinate to $u=\cos\theta$. Put $q=1-u^2$, $S=r^2+a^2u^2$, $D=r^2-2Mr+a^2$, and $A=r^2+a^2$. In coordinate order $(t,\phi,r,u)$ the metric is block diagonal between $(t,\phi)$ and $(r,u)$: $g=G\oplus h$, where $G=S^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}2Mr-S&-2Marq\\-2Marq&q(A^2-a^2Dq)\end{pmatrix}$ and $h=\operatorname{diag}(S/D,S/q)$. Direct $2\times2$ inversion gives $G^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}-(A^2-a^2Dq)/(SD)&-2Mar/(SD)\\-2Mar/(SD)&(D-a^2q)/(SDq)\end{pmatrix}$, with $\det G=-Dq$; the inverse base block is $h^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(D/S,q/S)$.

The derivatives needed below are $S_r=2r$, $S_u=2a^2u$, $S_{rr}=2$, $S_{ru}=0$, $S_{uu}=2a^2$, $D_r=2(r-M)$, $D_{rr}=2$, $q_u=-2u$, and $q_{uu}=-2$. On this chart $S,D,q>0$, so every denominator in the metric and inverse block is nonzero.

Write Greek indices $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ for $t,\phi$ and Latin indices $i,j,k,\ell$ for $r,u$. Since $G,h$ are independent of $t,\phi$, the complete nonzero Christoffel families from [F3] are $$\Gamma^\alpha{}_{\beta i}=\Gamma^\alpha{}_{i\beta}=\frac12(G^{-1})^{\alpha\gamma}\partial_iG_{\gamma\beta},\qquad \Gamma^i{}_{\alpha\beta}=-\frac12(h^{-1})^{ij}\partial_jG_{\alpha\beta},\qquad \Gamma^i{}_{jk}=\frac12(h^{-1})^{i\ell}(\partial_jh_{\ell k}+\partial_kh_{\ell j}-\partial_\ell h_{jk});$$ all families not forced by lower-index symmetry vanish. The six base coefficients, making the last family explicit, are $$\Gamma^r{}_{rr}=\frac rS-\frac{r-M}{D},\quad \Gamma^r{}_{ru}=\frac{a^2u}{S},\quad \Gamma^r{}_{uu}=-\frac{Dr}{Sq},\quad \Gamma^u{}_{rr}=-\frac{a^2uq}{SD},\quad \Gamma^u{}_{ru}=\frac rS,\quad \Gamma^u{}_{uu}=\frac{a^2u}{S}+\frac uq.$$ Thus the first two matrix families are fully specified by the displayed $G,G^{-1},h^{-1}$ and their $r,u$ derivatives, rather than by omitted connection coefficients.

Put $W_r:=(r-M)/D$, $W_u:=-u/q$, and $P_i:=G^{-1}\partial_iG$. Since $\partial_i\det G=(\det G)\operatorname{tr}(G^{-1}\partial_iG)$ and $\det G=-Dq$, the fiber connection trace is $\Gamma^\alpha{}_{\alpha i}=W_i$. Also $\det h=S^2/(Dq)$ and hence $\sqrt{|\det G\det h|}=S$. Substitution of the connection families in step 2.1 into the signed coordinate formula [F5], followed by the contraction $\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=R^a{}_{bad}$ of [F4], gives
$$\operatorname{Ric}_{\alpha\beta}=-\frac1{2S}\partial_i\!\left(S h^{ij}\partial_jG_{\alpha\beta}\right)+\frac12h^{ij}\left(\partial_iG\,G^{-1}\partial_jG\right)_{\alpha\beta},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{\alpha i}=0,$$
$$\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}=\operatorname{Ric}(h)_{ij}-\partial_iW_j+\Gamma^k{}_{ij}W_k-\frac14\operatorname{tr}(P_iP_j).$$
Indeed, for the fiber contraction the derivative and connection-trace terms are $\partial_i\Gamma^i{}_{\alpha\beta}+(\Gamma^k{}_{ki}+W_i)\Gamma^i{}_{\alpha\beta}$; combining them gives the divergence with volume factor $S$, while the two mixed-block quadratic terms give the displayed matrix product. In the base contraction, the base-only terms are $\operatorname{Ric}(h)_{ij}$, the fiber trace contributes $-\partial_iW_j+\Gamma^k{}_{ij}W_k$, and the remaining two mixed-block products give $-\tfrac14\operatorname{tr}(P_iP_j)$. Each mixed contraction vanishes from the listed connection families and $\partial_\alpha G=\partial_\alpha h=0$.
Using the six base coefficients in step 2.1 in the two-dimensional Ricci formula gives
$$\operatorname{Ric}(h)_{rr}=\frac{Mr(3a^2u^2-r^2)}{S^2D},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}(h)_{ru}=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}(h)_{uu}=\frac{Mr(3a^2u^2-r^2)}{S^2q}.$$
For clarity, set $H_{ij}:=-\partial_iW_j+\Gamma^k{}_{ij}W_k$ and $T_{ij}:=\tfrac14\operatorname{tr}(P_iP_j)$. For $(r,r)$, put $P_{rr}=M^2a^2u^2+3M^2r^2-2Ma^2ru^2-Ma^2r-3Mr^3+a^2r^2u^2+r^4$ and $Q_{rr}=M^2a^4u^4-2M^2a^2r^2u^2+5M^2r^4-2Ma^4ru^4+2Ma^4ru^2-2Ma^2r^3u^2-2Ma^2r^3-4Mr^5+a^4r^2u^4+2a^2r^4u^2+r^6$. Direct substitution gives $H_{rr}=P_{rr}/(SD^2)$ and $T_{rr}=Q_{rr}/(S^2D^2)$, so
$$\operatorname{Ric}_{rr}=\frac{Mr(3a^2u^2-r^2)D+SP_{rr}-Q_{rr}}{S^2D^2}=0.$$
For $(r,u)$, put $B=-Ma^2u^2+Ma^2-2Mr^2+a^2ru^2+r^3$. Direct substitution gives $H_{ru}=T_{ru}=-uB/(qSD)$, while $\operatorname{Ric}(h)_{ru}=0$, so $\operatorname{Ric}_{ru}=0$. For $(u,u)$, put $P_{uu}=-Mru^2+Mr+a^2u^4+r^2u^2$ and $Q_{uu}=u^2(-4Ma^2ru^2+4Ma^2r+a^4u^4+2a^2r^2u^2+r^4)$. Then $H_{uu}=P_{uu}/(q^2S)$ and $T_{uu}=Q_{uu}/(q^2S^2)$, whence
$$\operatorname{Ric}_{uu}=\frac{Mr(3a^2u^2-r^2)q+SP_{uu}-Q_{uu}}{q^2S^2}=0.$$
Both displayed numerators vanish by expansion using $S=r^2+a^2u^2$, $D=r^2-2Mr+a^2$, and $q=1-u^2$. These expressions include the derivative, trace, and quadratic-connection contributions with the signed convention [F4]-[F5].

In the fiber formula of step 3.1, $S h^{rr}=D$ and $S h^{uu}=q$. Define
$$\mathcal C_r:=-\frac1{2S}\partial_r(D\,\partial_rG)+\frac{D}{2S}(\partial_rG)G^{-1}(\partial_rG),\qquad \mathcal C_u:=-\frac1{2S}\partial_u(q\,\partial_uG)+\frac{q}{2S}(\partial_uG)G^{-1}(\partial_uG).$$
Thus $(\operatorname{Ric}_{\alpha\beta})_{\alpha,\beta=t,\phi}=\mathcal C_r+\mathcal C_u$. Put $z:=u^2$ and
$$U:=-4Mrz-a^2z^2+3a^2z+3r^2z-r^2,\qquad V:=4Ma^2rz-3a^4z-3a^2r^2z+a^2r^2+r^4,$$
$$Z:=-8M^2a^4r^2z^2+8M^2a^4r^2z-2Ma^6rz^3+4Ma^6rz^2-6Ma^6rz-2Ma^4r^3z^2-8Ma^4r^3z+2Ma^4r^3-8Ma^2r^5z+4Ma^2r^5+a^8z^3+a^6r^2z^3+3a^6r^2z^2+3a^4r^4z^2+3a^4r^4z+3a^2r^6z+a^2r^6+r^8.$$
Substituting the explicit $G,G^{-1}$ of step 1.1 and differentiating entrywise gives the three independent entries
$$\mathcal C_r=\frac1{S^4}\begin{pmatrix}2Ma^2rU&2MarqV\\2MarqV&-qZ\end{pmatrix},\qquad \mathcal C_u=-\frac1{S^4}\begin{pmatrix}2Ma^2rU&2MarqV\\2MarqV&-qZ\end{pmatrix}.$$
The $tt$, $t\phi$, and $\phi\phi$ entries therefore cancel separately. The mixed entries are zero by step 3.1, and all three base entries are zero by the component identities there. Hence every component of the Ricci tensor vanishes on the axis-avoiding polar chart, with no scalar-curvature shortcut.

The polar chart omits only the axis. By [A1] and [F2], $g$ is smooth there, and [F4]-[F5] make $\operatorname{Ric}(g)$ a smooth tensor. Since its components vanish on the dense axis-avoiding set by step 4.1, continuity makes $\operatorname{Ric}(g)$ vanish on the axis as well.
Thus $\operatorname{Ric}(g)=0$ at every point with $r>r_+$. The calculation proves a tensor identity for this specified metric; no Einstein field equation or classification of other metrics was used.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the tangent-bundle smooth structure of the
Lorentzian conventions.

Let $M>0$ and $a\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $|a|<M$, and put
$r_\pm:=M\pm\sqrt{M^2-a^2}$.

Let $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}:=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$ carry the
product smooth structure, where $S^2=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:x^2+y^2+z^2=1\}$
has its usual smooth structure and round metric $\gamma_{S^2}$. Let
$\pi:\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}\to S^2$ be the third projection, let $\xi$ be the
smooth rotation field on $S^2$ generated by $(x,y,z)\mapsto(-y,x,0)$, and put
$\gamma:=\pi^*\gamma_{S^2}$ and
$\xi^\flat:=\pi^*(\gamma_{S^2}(\xi,\cdot))$. Let $t,r$ be the first and
second coordinate functions on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$, and let
$\zeta:=z\circ\pi$ be the third Euclidean coordinate on the sphere factor.
Define the global smooth functions

$$\Sigma:=r^2+a^2\zeta^2,\qquad \Delta:=r^2-2Mr+a^2.$$

On a polar chart $0<\theta<\pi$, $\phi\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, one has
$\zeta=\cos\theta$, $\Sigma=r^2+a^2\cos^2\theta$,
$\gamma=d\theta^2+\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2$, and
$\xi^\flat=\sin^2\theta\,d\phi$.

Define the symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $g$ globally on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}$
by

$$g=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt\otimes dt+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr\otimes dr+\Sigma\gamma+\frac{a^2(\Sigma+2Mr)}{\Sigma}\,\xi^\flat\otimes\xi^\flat-\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma}\left(dt\otimes\xi^\flat+\xi^\flat\otimes dt\right).$$

Its Boyer-Lindquist line element on the polar chart is

$$ds^2=-\left(1-\frac{2Mr}{\Sigma}\right)dt^2-\frac{4Mar\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\,dt\,d\phi+\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr^2+\Sigma\,d\theta^2+\frac{(r^2+a^2)^2-a^2\Delta\sin^2\theta}{\Sigma}\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2.$$

The displayed cross term is $2g_{t\phi}\,dt\,d\phi$. This definition makes
no nondegeneracy or signature claim; Lorentzian signature and a time orientation
are established separately.

For $M>0$, $|a|<M$, and the Kerr exterior tensor datum, define
$T:=\partial_t$, $\Phi:=\xi$, $A:=r^2+a^2$, and $q:=\gamma(\xi,\xi)$.
The global vector field
$$N:=\frac{A^2-a^2\Delta q}{\Sigma\Delta}\,T+\frac{2aMr}{\Sigma\Delta}\,\Phi$$
is smooth; the tensor $g$ is smooth, symmetric, nondegenerate, and has
signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on all of
$\mathcal M_{\mathrm K}=\mathbb R\times(r_+,\infty)\times S^2$; and
$N=-\sharp_g(dt)$ is timelike. Thus $N$ defines a time orientation of this
Lorentzian four-manifold.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. Tensoriality of $R$ is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a).
Lowering its output slot with the smooth metric and contracting with the
smooth inverse metric are intrinsic tensor operations
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] clauses (b)-(c),
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]]). Thus these formulas give smooth
fields of types $(0,4)$, $(0,2)$, $(0,0)$ and $(0,2)$, respectively,
independent of the chart. Symmetry of $\operatorname{Ric}$ and $G$ is proved
separately in [[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clause (d).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let $R$ be
the curvature operator of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
with components $R^a{}_{bcd}$ in a chart.

**(a) Tensoriality.** For all smooth functions $f$ on $M$ and smooth vector
fields $X,Y,Z$ on a common domain, $R(X,Y)Z=-R(Y,X)Z$ and
$$R(fX,Y)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,fY)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,Y)(fZ)=fR(X,Y)Z .$$
Consequently, for every $p\in M$, the value $R(X,Y)Z|_p$ depends only on
$X_p,Y_p,Z_p$, and $R$ is a smooth tensor field of type $(1,3)$ on $M$ whose
components in every smooth chart are the functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ of
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]] clause (b).

**(b) Coordinate formula.** In every smooth chart $(U,x)$ with Christoffel
symbols $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ of $\nabla$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]),
$$R^a{}_{bcd}=\partial_c\Gamma^a{}_{db}-\partial_d\Gamma^a{}_{cb} +\sum_e\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{ce}\Gamma^e{}_{db}-\Gamma^a{}_{de}\Gamma^e{}_{cb}\bigr)$$
on $U$, for all $a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2,3\}$.

**(c) Point-normal formula.** If the chart is point-normal at $p$, that is
$g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}$, $\partial_ag_{bc}(p)=0$ and $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(p)=0$
([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]), then, writing
$g_{ad,bc}:=\partial_b\partial_cg_{ad}$,
$$R_{abcd}(p)=\tfrac12\bigl(g_{ad,bc}+g_{bc,ad}-g_{bd,ac}-g_{ac,bd}\bigr)(p) .$$
Equivalently, $R^a{}_{bcd}(p)=\tfrac12\,g^{ae}(p)\bigl(\partial_b\partial_cg_{ed}
+\partial_e\partial_dg_{bc}-\partial_e\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_b\partial_dg_{ec}\bigr)(p)$.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $c>0$ be a fixed conversion constant in metres per second. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval of physical time in seconds, and let $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}=\mathbb R^3/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^3$ have dimensionless angular coordinates $x^1,x^2,x^3$. Its quotient charts are local lifts to $\mathbb R^3$; chart changes are translations by elements of $(2\pi\mathbb Z)^3$. Give $M=I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ the product smooth structure, so $M$ is a smooth four-manifold without boundary. Here a **$C^2$ time-oriented Lorentzian metric datum** means a symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $g$ with $C^2$ components in smooth charts, whose value at each point has inertia $(3,1,0)$, together with a smooth vector field $N$ satisfying $g(N,N)<0$ everywhere. This is the explicit $C^2$ variant of the pointwise signature and time-orientation conditions in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; that supplier's metric regularity itself is smooth. Choose positive $C^2$ functions $a_i:I\to(0,\infty)$, $i=1,2,3$, with values in metres, and set

$$g=-c^2\,dt^2+\sum_{i=1}^3a_i(t)^2\,(dx^i)^2,\qquad N:=\partial_t.$$

In every lifted product chart, $g$ has matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-c^2,a_1^2,a_2^2,a_3^2)$, so it is symmetric, $C^2$, and has inertia $(3,1,0)$; $N$ is smooth and $g(N,N)=-c^2<0$. Thus $(M,g,N)$ is a $C^2$ time-oriented Lorentzian metric datum in the stated sense. This diagonal, spatially homogeneous metric datum is called a diagonal Bianchi I datum here; homogeneity means its coefficients are independent of the torus coordinates, and no isotropy is required. Define the directional expansion rates, their mean, the spatial volume scale and the squared directional shear by

$$H_i:=\frac{\dot a_i}{a_i},\qquad H:=\frac13\sum_{i=1}^3H_i,\qquad V:=a_1a_2a_3,\qquad \sigma^2:=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^3(H_i-H)^2.$$

Here $\dot a_i=d a_i/dt$; $H_i$ and $H$ have units $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, $V$ has units $\mathrm{m}^3$, and $\sigma^2$ has units $\mathrm{s}^{-2}$. The symbol $\sigma^2$ denotes a nonnegative scalar defined by this formula, not a tensor norm on a spacetime frame. This is a geometric ansatz and makes no field-equation or observational claim. The product and quotient constructions carry the inherited axiom of countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and use no stronger choice principle.

For comparison with smooth Lorentzian geometry, use the curvature convention $R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$ and the component order $R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=R^a{}_{bcd}\partial_a$. The local connection and Ricci components for this $C^2$ metric are defined separately.

Let $M$ be an oriented smooth four-manifold and let $\phi$ be a field
configuration in a specified smooth field bundle. A **local Lagrangian
four-form** $\mathcal L(\phi)$ is a smooth four-form whose coordinate
coefficients depend smoothly on the field components and finitely many
spacetime derivatives at each point. A **chosen first-variation
decomposition** consists of a linear Euler functional $E_\phi[\eta]$ with
values in four-forms and a three-form $\theta(\phi;\eta)$, each linear in the
field variation $\eta$ and its derivatives, such that every smooth
one-parameter field family satisfies

$$\delta\mathcal L=E_\phi[\delta\phi]+d_M\theta(\phi;\delta\phi).$$

The choice is part of the data; it is not asserted to be unique. In a
parameter family, $\delta_iE_\phi$ means the derivative of the coefficients
of $E_\phi$ with its variation input held fixed. Thus the total derivative of
$E_{\phi(p)}[\eta(p)]$ is
$(\delta_iE_\phi)[\eta]+E_\phi[\delta_i\eta]$. For a smooth
finite-dimensional field family with parameter exterior derivative $d_P$,
the one-form $\Theta$ on parameter space with values in spacetime three-forms
is $\Theta_p(v)=\theta(\phi_p;\delta_v\phi_p)$. Define the **covariant
presymplectic current** by $\omega:=-d_P\Theta$. For commuting parameter
coordinates $s_1,s_2$ this is

For a finite oriented smooth singular three-chain $\Sigma$, define the

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold and let $\pi:E\to M$ be a smooth fibre
bundle. A **field configuration** is a smooth section $\phi:M\to E$, so
$\pi\circ\phi=\operatorname{id}_M$. For a finite-dimensional smooth manifold

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle and tetrad
conventions of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and
[[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth,
time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, let
$U\subseteq M$ be nonempty and open, and let
$E=(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ be a smooth future-directed tetrad on $U$. Thus the
$E_J$ are a pointwise basis of $TM|_U$, $g(E_I,E_J)=\eta_{IJ}$ for
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and $E_0$ is future-directed. Write
$e=(e^0,e^1,e^2,e^3)^{\mathsf T}$ for the dual coframe, so
$e^I(E_J)=\delta^I{}_J$.

A **tetrad connection** is a smooth affine connection $\nabla$ on $TM|_U$;
its connection matrix $\omega=(\omega^I{}_J)$ in $E$ is defined by
$\nabla_XE_J=\sum_I\omega^I{}_J(X)E_I$. It is a **Lorentz connection** when
it is metric-compatible, equivalently when the matrix-valued one-form is
$\eta$-skew: $\omega_{IJ}:=\eta_{IK}\omega^K{}_J$ satisfies
$\omega_{IJ}=-\omega_{JI}$. A smooth local Lorentz change is a smooth map
$\Lambda:U\to SO^+(1,3)$. With the convention
$e'=\Lambda e$ (equivalently $E'=E\Lambda^{-1}$), the connection matrix
transforms as

$$e'=\Lambda e,\qquad \omega'=\Lambda\omega\Lambda^{-1}-d\Lambda\,\Lambda^{-1}.$$

Here $d$ is the componentwise exterior derivative, and products of
matrix-valued forms use matrix multiplication and the wedge product of their
scalar form entries. Define the torsion and curvature forms by

$$T^I:=de^I+\sum_J\omega^I{}_J\wedge e^J,\qquad F^I{}_J:=d\omega^I{}_J+\sum_K\omega^I{}_K\wedge\omega^K{}_J.$$

Thus $T$ is an $\mathbb R^4$-valued two-form and $F$ is an
$\operatorname{End}(\mathbb R^4)$-valued two-form. With this convention,
$F$ is the local curvature two-form of $\nabla$. A local $\Lambda$ is a
change of frame in a trivialization; it represents a gauge transformation in
the sense of [[def-gauge-group-of-a-smooth-principal-bundle]] only when it
extends to a principal-bundle automorphism over the identity. No such extension,
global tetrad, or spin structure is part of this definition.

For transport as in [[def-gr-fx-connection-path-transport]], with composition convention $[\delta]\circ[\gamma]=[\delta*\gamma]$ meaning first traverse $\gamma$ and then $\delta$,

$$U_{\delta*\gamma}(1)=U_\delta(1)U_\gamma(1),\qquad U_{\bar\gamma}(1)=U_\gamma(1)^{-1}.$$

Let $E=(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ be the tetrad of [[def-gr-fx-connection-path-transport]]. For each $x\in U$, let $E_x:\mathbb R^4\to T_xM$ send the standard basis vector $\mathbf e_I$ to $E_I(x)$; because the tetrad vectors are a basis, $E_x$ is an invertible real-linear map, hence a linear isomorphism ([[def-linear-isomorphism-and-invertible-linear-map]]). A groupoid is a category in which every morphism is an isomorphism ([[def-isomorphism-groupoid-and-connected-category]]). Define the target groupoid $\mathcal T(U)$ to have base-point-tagged objects $\tau_x:=(x,T_xM)$ for $x\in U$ and morphisms $\tau_x\to\tau_y$ the tagged triples $(\tau_x,\tau_y,L)$ where $L:T_xM\to T_yM$ is a real-linear isomorphism; identities and composition are tagged identity maps and ordinary composition ([[def-category]]). A covariant functor assigns objects and morphisms and preserves identities and composition ([[def-functor-and-contravariant-functor]]). The functor from the thin path groupoid [[def-gr-fx-thin-path-groupoid]] to $\mathcal T(U)$ sends $x$ to $\tau_x$ and sends $[\gamma]:x\to y$ to the tagged tangent-space arrow

$$\bigl(\tau_x,\tau_y,E_y\,U_\gamma(1)\,E_x^{-1}\bigr):\tau_x\longrightarrow\tau_y.$$

Here $U_\gamma(1)$ acts on tetrad components, while $E_y$ and $E_x^{-1}$ convert between components and tangent vectors. Under the supplier convention $e'=\Lambda e$, the component matrix in the changed local frame satisfies

$$U'_{\gamma}(1)=\Lambda(\gamma(1))U_\gamma(1)\Lambda(\gamma(0))^{-1}.$$

Let $M$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, $U\subseteq M$ a nonempty open set with a smooth tetrad, and $\omega$ its Lorentz-connection matrix from [[def-gr-fx-tetrad-spin-connection]]. Assume the supplier's $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention. For a piecewise-smooth path $\gamma:[0,1]\to U$, let $A_\gamma(t)=\omega_{\gamma(t)}(\dot\gamma(t))$ on each smooth piece. By Proposition [[prop-gr-fx-connection-path-transport-exists]], there is a unique continuous piecewise-$C^1$ solution

$$\dot U_\gamma(t)=-A_\gamma(t)U_\gamma(t),\qquad U_\gamma(0)=I_4.$$

The endpoint matrix $U_\gamma(1)$ is the **connection path transport** in the chosen tetrad trivialization. It maps vector components at $\gamma(0)$ to components at $\gamma(1)$ under the convention of the supplier. A smooth local Lorentz frame change transforms this matrix by its endpoint frame matrices; it is a gauge transformation in the principal-bundle sense only if it extends to an automorphism over the identity as in [[def-gauge-group-of-a-smooth-principal-bundle]].

derivations.claim: Set $A=\omega_i(p)$ and $B=\omega_j(p)$. The integral equation $U(t)=I-\int_0^t\omega(\dot\gamma)U$ gives the positive-$i$ segment expansion $S_1=I-\varepsilon A+\tfrac12\varepsilon^2(A^2-\partial_iA)+O(\varepsilon^3)$. On the following positive-$j$ segment, Taylor expansion at $p+\varepsilon e_i$ gives $S_2=I-\varepsilon B+\varepsilon^2(\tfrac12B^2-\partial_iB-\tfrac12\partial_jB)+O(\varepsilon^3)$. In each case the second iterated integral contributes $\tfrac12\varepsilon^2\omega_k(p)^2$, and the first integral contributes the displayed derivative terms.

Along the negative-$i$ segment from $p+\varepsilon e_i+\varepsilon e_j$ to $p+\varepsilon e_j$ and the negative-$j$ segment from $p+\varepsilon e_j$ to $p$, the same integral expansion gives $S_3=I+\varepsilon A+\varepsilon^2(\tfrac12A^2+\tfrac12\partial_iA+\partial_jA)+O(\varepsilon^3)$ and $S_4=I+\varepsilon B+\tfrac12\varepsilon^2(B^2+\partial_jB)+O(\varepsilon^3)$. The derivative terms use starting points $p+\varepsilon e_j$ and $p$; reversing the tangent changes the first-order ODE coefficient's sign.

For any fixed $q$, uniqueness in [F1] shows that adjoining a segment with identity-initial transport $S$ to an already traversed path with transport $T$ gives total matrix $ST$: $S(t)T$ solves the next segment's ODE with its required initial value. Applying this successively gives total transport $S_4S_3S_2S_1$; for $q=4$ this agrees with [F3]. Its linear terms cancel. The within-segment quadratic terms sum to $A^2+B^2-\partial_iB+\partial_jA$; the six cross-products sum to $BA-B^2-BA-AB-A^2+BA=BA-AB-A^2-B^2$. The full coefficient is therefore $\partial_jA-\partial_iB+BA-AB=-(\partial_i\omega_j-\partial_j\omega_i+[A,B])=-F_{ij}(p)$ by [F2]. For a uniform remainder, choose a compact neighborhood $K'$ of $K$ contained in $V$ and containing the four square sides for $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0$; the $C^2$ coefficients and derivatives are bounded there. Taylor remainders in single integrals are uniformly $O(\varepsilon^3)$, and if $M$ bounds coefficient norms in the fixed submultiplicative norm, iterated-integral terms of order $m\ge3$ are bounded by $M^m\varepsilon^m/m!$, whose sum is $O(\varepsilon^3)$. Multiplying four expansions preserves the uniform remainder order.
